newsitem.title: USA: Vivus settles patent license lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Vivus settles patent license lawsuit.

text.p: Vivus Inc said Tuesday that it has settled a lawsuit filed in Texas by the licensors from whom the company acquired a patent license.
Vivus said that under the settlement agreement, the licensors agreed to dismiss their lawsuit against the company, its chairman, and president and chief executive officer.
Each side agreed to release any claims it alleges to have against the other and the licensors will not receive any compensation from Vivus or its executives.

Vivus said it will continue to pay royalties to the licensors based on sales of the company's MUSE (alprostadil) product for erectile dysfunction pursuant to the terms of the December 1992 license agreement between the parties.

According to Vivus, the licensors had alleged that they were defrauded in connection with the negotiations that led to the execution of a new license agreement between the company and the licensors in December 1992.
